questions.stem: Why do alcohols have higher boiling points than alkanes of similar molecular mass?

options.text: Alcohols have stronger covalent bonds within their molecules
Alcohols have more electrons than alkanes
Alcohols can form hydrogen bonds between their -OH groups

questions.explanation: The -OH group in alcohols is polar, allowing alcohol molecules to form hydrogen bonds with each other. These hydrogen bonds are stronger than the London dispersion forces between alkane molecules, so more energy is needed to separate the molecules, resulting in higher boiling points.
